text:
ana: Quick heads-up: we're opening a preview for Private 2.6 that introduces two customer-requested features: a bring-your-own-control-plane (BYOC) option and fine-grained data residency toggles (region-level routing + local logging). Preview signup will be limited; details below. :sparkles:

sam: Security highlight: BYOC mode lets customers run the control plane endpoints in their VPC while still using Redwood-managed runtime images. Network model requires mutual TLS and customer-provisioned certs. We'll publish the threat model and recommended ACLs.

jia: Ops/installer note: BYOC requires an extra bootstrap token and a control-plane manifest to be applied by the customer. We'll provide a reference deploy script for common K8s distros and an airgap-friendly bundle. Pilot capacity: 8 customers. Signup: https://confluence.redwood/internal/private/2.6-byoc-preview (internal).

laura: Legal/comms: approved external phrasing will be "Private preview: customer-controlled control-plane (BYOC) available by request; compliance artifacts available under NDA." Do not say "managed control plane" for BYOC. We'll draft a short FAQ for sales and CSMs.

maria: CS play: offering 8 hours of migration assistance for preview customers. CSMs, collect control-plane hostnames, cert process (ACME/PKI), and any PCI or HIPAA scope flags up front.

ryan: Sales: can we get a one-pager summarizing what BYOC enables (reduced audit surface for customers, local audit logs, separate billing pipes)? Also flag any pricing delta for BYOC.

dena: Product note: data residency toggles let customers enforce where embeddings and cached prompts are stored (region tags: us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). Control plane metadata remains minimal when BYOC is used. We'll include a per-tenant residency policy API.

oliver: Ops rollout plan: preview will be strictly opt-in. Canary plan for hosted will not apply; BYOC customers are isolated. For on-prem customers, provide signed bundles and a verification checklist. Oncall for preview: @oliver primary, @jia backup. Runbook: /runbooks/private-2.6-byoc-preview.md

security-bot: "policy: byoc-preview bootstrap token created by jia at 2026-06-10T09:12:00Z"

sam: Security checklist (short): require customer-side firewall rules to only allow control-plane egress to Redwood runtime registries, enforce mTLS, restrict admin API keys to short-lived sessions, and enable per-tenant key wrap. We'll post the full security guide.

jia: Example BYOC bootstrap (internal docs snippet):

```bash
# run on customer's control plane host
rwinf-bootstrap --mode byoc \ 
  --tenant T-67890 \ 
  --bootstrap-token <token> \ 
  --control-plane-host cp.example.internal \ 
  --accept-eula
```

laura: Compliance note: preview includes PCI scoping guidance but does NOT imply PCI attestation. Use careful language: "PCI scoping assistance available under engagement." I'll draft the FAQ language.

maria: CSMs 9: please prepare a short outbound note for impacted accounts and include migration options. We'll hold an office hour during week 1 of the preview.

oliver: Ops checklist: require signed bundle verification, snapshot before onboarding, enable verbose logs for 24h post-onboard, collect perf counters every 1m for first 6h.

ryan: Flagging two enterprise prospects who asked for BYOC; cc @maria @laura. We should prioritize one for early access if legal clears.

ana (ana correction): small edit 9: preview is BYOC + residency toggles in 2.6-rc1; other features (e.g., PCI templates) are staged in a follow-up patch.

deploy-bot: "scheduled: private-2.6-byoc-preview kickoff 2026-06-17T16:00Z"

ana: Internal walkthrough + Q&A next Wed 10:00 PT. We'll demo the BYOC bootstrap, residency API, and the control-plane manifest. Please RSVP if you're supporting preview customers. If you're not in the preview, react with :eyes: and we'll share the recording. Thanks all!
